newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian avg lending rate rises to 12.7 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian avg lending rate rises to 12.7 pct.

text.p: The Croatian average lending rate rose to 12.7 percent on Friday from 10 percent, boosted by stronger demand for term loans.
Dealers put total trade at 48.3 million kuna against a 58 million demand.
Interbank call money at a steady 10 percent accounted for 19 million of the total. The rest were term deals, some of which were renewed by lenders upon expiry.

Term rates ranged between 14 and 16.5 percent for two-week and 30-day loans. Savings banks paid 11 percent for six-day and 18 percent for two-month funds -- slightly higher than what is charged to banks due to their perceived repayment risk.
The central bank calculated its kuna midrates for Saturday and next Monday weaker at 3.5686 against the dollar and firmer at 6.1630 against the German mark.
